newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Most grains futures slip in high Budapest turnover.
newsitem.headline: Most grains futures slip in high Budapest turnover.

text.p: Most grains futures on the Budapest Commodity Exchange dived on Wednesday except for virtually untraded sunflowerseed contracts, dealers said.
"The Hungarian grains market is five to ten times as hectic as the world market," said Ferenc Kiss of Agrokont.
He said this was due to the fact that information was almost completely lacking in the disorganised agricultural sector.
"We are talking about a wheat surplus but nobody knows how much it is or where exactly it is," Kiss said.
Consequently, if a major market player starts selling or buying, others follow suit, he said.
"The market's reaction is: if he sells (or buys) he must have some solid information that we do not have, so we had better do the same," he said.
This has led to March milling wheat price dropping to 24,300 forints per tonne, compared with 1996 August spot prices of 26,000 forints.
Maize prices for the 1997 crop, in the region of 18,600 forints, were already around production prices, but it was hard to give any long-term forecasts, he said.

"We know little about how this year's agricultural subsidies (of some 100 billion forints) would be spent," he said. "But the government is bound to do something to please farmers because elections are getting closer".
Hungary's Prime Minister Gyula Horn indicated May 1998 as a suitable time for general elections.

Total grains futures turnover was 2,166 contracts or 814 million forints, of which 1,117 were maize contracts while milling wheat and feed wheat accounted for most of the rest. --Denes Albert, Budapest newsroom +36 1 327 4040 ($=170.30 Hungarian forints) Lot size is 20,000 kgs for all contracts.
